text.p: Oman oil output averaged 323,029,000 barrels (885,010 barrels per day) in 1996, up from 852,700 bpd the year before, according to figures released by Oman's Ministry of Development.
Crude exports from the non-OPEC Gulf Arab state reached 811,476 bpd last year from 779,800 bpd in 1995.
Japan was Oman's largest customer, taking an average of 247,926 bpd, followed by South Korea with 156,068 bpd.
Oman crude averaged $19.42, up from $16.39 in 1995.
Refinery runs ran at 73,128 bpd in 1996, up from 72,712 bpd in 1995 while product output totalled 70,572 bpd down from 70,657 bpd, the ministry's monthly statistical bulletin showed.

Output of super (97 octane) gasoline totalled 3,893,000 barrels in 1996, regular (90 octane) 996,000 barrels, jet-A1 1,250,700 barrels, gas oil 5,261,700 barrels, long residue 13,973,100 barrels and butane 384,300 barrels.
Oil and gas revenue represented 77.1 percent of government revenue on a preliminary basis.
